interview_questions.q: How do you prevent hallucinations in a production RAG chatbot?
interview_questions.a: Multi-layer approach: (1) Retrieve from verified knowledge base (RAG eliminates reliance on LLM training data). (2) Include source citations in every response so users can verify. (3) Confidence threshold — if retrieved context similarity score is below threshold, decline to answer rather than guess. (4) Output validation with Pydantic models to detect malformed or implausible responses. (5) RAGAS evaluation metrics (faithfulness, answer relevance, context recall) measured before every deployment.

interview_questions.q: What's your approach to chatbot conversation memory at scale?
interview_questions.a: Short-term (in-session): last N messages in LLM context window. Long-term (cross-session): PostgreSQL for message archive. Active session state in Redis for sub-millisecond retrieval. Context compression: when conversation exceeds context window, summarize earlier turns rather than truncate. Session management: JWT-based user association. At millions of conversations: time-based database partitioning + async archiving.

interview_questions.q: How do you evaluate RAG chatbot quality before launching to production?
interview_questions.a: RAGAS evaluation suite: faithfulness (does the answer match retrieved context?), answer relevance (does the answer address the question?), context recall (was the right context retrieved?), context precision. Build a golden dataset of 200+ representative Q&A pairs covering all knowledge base topics. Run automated RAGAS evaluation on every deployment. Set minimum score thresholds — below which the chatbot does not go to production. Measure latency at p50/p95/p99 under realistic load.

interview_questions.q: How do you architect a chatbot for multiple languages?
interview_questions.a: Modern LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) natively handle 100+ languages — no separate models per language. For RAG: use multilingual embedding models (multilingual-e5-large or OpenAI's text-embedding-3-large) so English knowledge base retrieves correctly for Spanish/French/Japanese queries. Language detection in middleware — route to language-appropriate escalation agents. Evaluate retrieval quality per target language in RAGAS before launch. One backend, one knowledge base, true multilingual capability.
